metaDescription: Odoo Helpdesk in practice: SLA policies counted in working hours, email alias threading, portal user cost, after-sales returns, and why it is Enterprise only.
intro: Odoo Helpdesk is an Enterprise application. There is no Helpdesk app in Community, and that single fact settles most helpdesk projects before anything else is discussed. What the licence buys is a ticket model living in the same database as the sale order, the delivery and the invoice, so an agent can see what the customer bought, what shipped late and what is still unpaid without leaving the ticket or asking another department.

The work in a helpdesk build is not the kanban board. It is the stage model, the SLA policies and the email path. Stages describe how the team actually works, SLA policies decide what counts as late, and the alias and catchall configuration decides whether a customer reply lands on the existing ticket or opens a second one. Those three decisions carry the project. Everything after them is data entry and training.

Cost follows the user model, and this is where budgets move. Agents are internal Odoo users and are billed per user. Customers who raise and follow tickets through the portal are portal users and are not billed at all. Support desks that give every client contact an internal account, usually because portal access looked fiddly in week one, end up paying a monthly licence for people who only ever read their own tickets.
whoFor: B2B suppliers working to contractual response and resolution times, where missing a target has a commercial consequence and somebody has to prove afterwards that the target was met.
Companies already running Odoo Sales and Inventory, where a complaint has to end in a return, a repair order or a credit note rather than in an email thread nobody can find later.
IT and equipment service providers billing support against a contract or a block of prepaid hours, since time logged on a ticket can flow through a sale order to an invoice.
Manufacturers and distributors handling warranty claims on serialised goods, where the lot number on the ticket has to match what was actually delivered to that customer.
Not for organisations committed to Odoo Community with no route to Enterprise, because the app is simply absent and rebuilding it in Project gives you tasks without an SLA engine.
Not for high volume contact centres that need call queueing, IVR, skills based routing and supervisor wallboards, none of which exist in standard Odoo.

capabilities.title: Teams carry almost every setting
capabilities.body: A helpdesk team is the unit that holds the email alias, the member list, the SLA policies, the after sales options, the help center and whether the portal is open. Stages belong to teams and can be shared by several, which is convenient until two teams need different closing rules on the same stage. Assignment is chosen per team as manual, random or balanced, where balanced hands the next ticket to the member with the fewest open ones. There is no skills based routing.

capabilities.title: SLA policies and how a deadline is actually calculated
capabilities.body: An SLA policy says that tickets matching a set of criteria, such as priority, tag, ticket type, customer or company, must reach a named stage within a number of working hours or days. Several policies can apply to one ticket at once and each is tracked separately with its own status on the record. The countdown runs against a working schedule rather than the wall clock, and stages can be excluded from it, which is how the clock stops while you wait for the customer to reply.

capabilities.title: The routes a ticket arrives by
capabilities.body: Four channels cover most deployments. An email alias per team turns support at your domain into tickets and threads later replies onto the same record. A website form gives structured fields instead of free text. The customer portal lets a signed in contact raise and follow tickets. Live Chat, on Enterprise, has a command that turns a conversation into a ticket with the transcript attached. Tickets can also be created by API or by an automation rule fired from another record.

capabilities.title: After sales actions that reach the rest of Odoo
capabilities.body: Each after sales option enabled on a team turns a ticket into a real transaction rather than a note. Refund raises a credit note against the original invoice. Return creates an incoming picking so goods come back into stock properly. Repair opens a repair order. Onsite intervention creates a Field Service task with the address and customer already filled in. Coupons issue a discount code as a goodwill gesture. Every one of them stays linked to the ticket, so the trail is one record.

capabilities.title: Support time, logged and billed
capabilities.body: With Timesheets switched on for a team, agents log hours directly on the ticket. If the team is also set to bill that time, the ticket links to a sale order line and the hours reach an invoice through ordinary service invoicing. Prepaid blocks of hours work the same way, with the balance visible on the order. Teams that never invoice support still gain from logging, because recorded hours are the only honest measure of what a fixed price contract costs to serve.

capabilities.title: A help center customers can use without you
capabilities.body: A team can publish a help center built from three optional pieces: Knowledge articles for procedures and answers, a website forum for public questions, and eLearning courses for onboarding material. Agents can insert a published article into a reply rather than retyping it. Articles that are not published stay internal, so the runbook the agent follows and the answer the customer reads can live in the same tree without the internal version leaking to the portal.

capabilities.title: Ratings and the reports that settle arguments
capabilities.body: A rating request can be sent when a ticket reaches a chosen stage, and the customer answers with a happy, neutral or unhappy face plus a comment. Those become rating records, the same structure Project uses, so satisfaction reporting needs no build. Standard analysis covers tickets, SLA status and ratings, sliced by team, agent, stage, tag and period. SLA status analysis is the report to put in front of a customer who insists you are always late.

setup.title: Fix the team structure before touching stages
setup.body: The team boundary is the expensive decision to reverse, because the alias, the SLA policies, the reporting and the member list all hang off it. Teams by product line work where the skills differ. Teams by region work where the working calendar and the language differ. Teams per customer almost never work, since the count keeps growing and each one needs its own alias and policies. Write the routing rule down first, then build the smallest number of teams that satisfies it.

setup.title: Wire the email path, then test the reply
setup.body: Set the alias domain and the catchall in system parameters, point an incoming mail server at the mailbox, then give each team its alias. On a self hosted server the mailbox must not rewrite headers, because reply threading depends on the message id and the reply address. Test three things before go live: a new mail creating a ticket, a customer reply landing on that same ticket, and an out of office auto reply failing to create a second one.

setup.title: Model stages around the SLA clock
setup.body: Stages that exist only to look busy make the SLA meaningless. Keep the set small and identify the stages where the ball is genuinely with the customer, because those are the ones to exclude from SLA counting. Decide which stage means first response and which means resolved, since those are what the policies will target. Fold the closed stages so the kanban stays readable, and agree in writing who may move a ticket backwards and what that does to the clock.

setup.title: Build the working schedule and the holidays
setup.body: A four hour SLA means nothing until the system knows which four hours. The working schedule driving the calculation has to match the real week, Sunday to Thursday across most of the Gulf, and it has to carry public holidays or targets will expire over Eid while the office is shut. Desks covering several countries need a schedule per calendar and a clear rule about which one applies. Contracts promising cover around the clock need a schedule that says exactly that.

setup.title: Open the portal to the right contacts
setup.body: Portal access is granted from the contact record, and a contact sees the tickets where they are the customer. Contacts under one company can be given a wider view through the commercial entity, which is what a client with five site managers actually wants. Decide early whether customers may close their own tickets, and read your stage names as a customer would, because the portal shows them. Rename anything that would be awkward on a client screen before launch.

setup.title: Agree what happens to the old tickets
setup.body: Importing history is heavier than it looks. Ticket bodies belong in the chatter as messages and attachments as their own records, and the original creation date is not exposed by the standard import screen, so keeping real timestamps needs a scripted load. SLA history cannot be recalculated afterwards, which means migrated tickets distort any comparison of before and after. Many projects import open tickets only and keep the old system readable for a year.

pitfalls.title: Budgeting for Helpdesk on Community
pitfalls.body: The app is Enterprise only, and the discovery usually happens after the project has been priced. The Community substitute is Project, configured with stages, a task type per issue, timesheets and portal sharing. That gives a queue and a customer view, but no SLA policy engine, no after sales actions from the ticket and no rating request on a stage change. Community modules exist and vary in quality. Decide which path you are on before kickoff, not during user testing.

pitfalls.title: Two tickets for every conversation
pitfalls.body: Duplicate tickets are the most common go live complaint and they are almost always the mail path. A forwarding rule that rewrites the sender breaks the customer match, a mailbox with its own auto responder answers the alias and creates a fresh ticket, and an agent replying from Outlook instead of the chatter starts a parallel thread the system cannot see. Fix the forwarding, then stop agents replying outside Odoo. The second half is training, not configuration.

pitfalls.title: Log note against send message
pitfalls.body: The chatter offers both and only one of them is private. A message reaches the followers of the ticket, which includes the portal customer once they are following it. Internal opinion typed as a message is then visible on the customer portal, permanently, with a timestamp against it. This causes more embarrassment than any technical defect on a helpdesk project. Train the distinction on day one and check the follower list on tickets created from inbound mail.

pitfalls.title: SLA policies that nobody can read
pitfalls.body: Two failures repeat. The first is overlap: four policies matching every ticket produces a status list an agent stops reading and a report nobody trusts. The second is timing, because a policy added after go live does not rewrite the history of tickets already open, so the first weeks of SLA reporting are not comparable with later ones. Start with one or two policies that match your actual contracts, and add more only when a real dispute needs the evidence.

pitfalls.title: Paying a licence for your customers
pitfalls.body: Client contacts given internal user accounts, usually to skip a portal invitation, are billed like employees. On a desk serving fifty companies with three contacts each, that is a large monthly line for people who read their own tickets and nothing else. Portal users cost nothing and see what they should see. The audit is quick: list the internal users, check which ones map to an employee record, and convert the rest before the next renewal.

pitfalls.title: Assuming escalation is a feature
pitfalls.body: There is no escalation matrix in the product. A breached SLA changes the status on the ticket and appears in reporting, but it does not notify a manager, reassign the work or telephone anybody. Escalation has to be assembled from stages, automation rules that notify or reassign, and scheduled activities with named owners. Define what escalation means in the contract you signed, then build that, rather than waiting for a switch labelled escalate to appear in the settings.

worksWith: Sales and Subscriptions, so an agent can check what the customer bought and whether the support contract is still running
Timesheets and Project, for logging support hours and turning them into a billable line
Field Service, so an onsite intervention raised from a ticket becomes a scheduled task with a worksheet
Repairs and Inventory, for warranty returns, spare parts and the serial number history of the delivered unit
Accounting, for the credit note that a refund action raises against the original invoice
Knowledge, Forum and eLearning, which together make up the customer facing help center
Live Chat, which converts a chat into a ticket with the transcript already attached
Studio and automation rules, for custom ticket fields and stage driven notifications without writing code

regional.note: The working schedule behind every SLA has to be Sunday to Thursday on Riyadh time, or each Friday ticket reports late and the numbers stop meaning anything. Arabic leads on the portal, the mail templates and the rating request, so right to left layout is checked before launch. Ticket attachments hold personal data covered by the Personal Data Protection Law, which makes retention a setting rather than an afterthought.

The UAE runs a Monday to Friday week with a short Friday, unlike its neighbours, and copying one Gulf SLA calendar across the region is a routine error on multi country rollouts. Annual maintenance revenue sits inside the 5 percent VAT and corporate tax net, so support contracts belong on subscriptions with proper invoices. Free zone and mainland entities usually need separate teams and separate aliases.

Sales tax on services is provincial, so a maintenance contract billed from tickets across Karachi and Lahore answers to SRB and PRA separately, at different rates, and the tax cannot follow the customer default. Many local firms still work a six day week, which is not the schedule an SLA template ships with. FBR digital invoicing applies the moment the support invoice is issued.

Support is a service, so place of supply decides IGST against CGST and SGST, and a ticket billed to a branch in another state is not the same invoice as one billed to head office. The support product needs its own service accounting code. Public holidays differ by state, so a single national holiday calendar makes SLA targets wrong in half your offices.

Records have to stay in Turkiye, and that includes ticket attachments, chatter messages and portal uploads sitting in the Odoo filestore, so hosting location is decided by law rather than by preference. KVKK expects a clarification text where data is collected, which means the portal ticket form and not only the privacy page. Support billing then splits between e-Fatura and e-Arsiv by counterparty.

Agent level reporting on response time and rating counts as performance monitoring under the Works Constitution Act, so a company with a works council settles a written agreement before those dashboards are published by name. Public holidays are set per Bundesland, which makes a single national SLA calendar wrong for a distributed team. Invoices raised from tickets fall under GoBD retention and the DATEV export the tax adviser expects.

A UK GDPR erasure request has to reach the ticket chatter and its attachments, not just the contact record, so agree who executes that and how it is evidenced before the first one arrives. Support and maintenance invoices raised from tickets stay inside Making Tax Digital, with digital links through to the VAT return. Public sector buyers ask whether the customer portal meets the accessibility regulations.

French consumer law does not allow a premium rate number for after sales or complaint handling, so the contact details published on the portal and inside ticket emails need checking against that. Customer facing templates are expected in French under the language rules for commercial content. The invoice that follows a billable ticket falls under the Factur-X reform, while the ticket itself does not.

faqs.q: Is Odoo Helpdesk available in Community?
faqs.a: No. Helpdesk is an Enterprise application with no Community equivalent. The usual substitute is Project, set up with stages, a task type per issue, timesheets and portal sharing. That covers the queue and the customer view, but not the SLA policy engine, the after sales actions raised from a ticket, or the rating request triggered by a stage change.

faqs.q: Do customers need a paid user account to raise tickets?
faqs.a: No. Customers use portal access, which is not billed. Agents, team leaders and anyone who needs the backend are internal users and are billed per user. Desks become expensive when client contacts are given internal accounts for convenience, so grant portal access from the contact record and keep internal accounts for your own staff.

faqs.q: Can the SLA clock stop while we wait for the customer?
faqs.a: Yes. An SLA policy can exclude stages, so a ticket parked in a stage such as waiting on customer does not burn its target. It only works if that stage exists and agents actually move tickets into it, which is a habit to train rather than a setting to switch on. Reporting on time spent in excluded stages is worth reviewing monthly.

faqs.q: Can we handle support over WhatsApp?
faqs.a: WhatsApp is a separate Enterprise application with its own configuration and a Meta business account behind it. It is not another inbox inside a helpdesk team, and messages do not become tickets by themselves. If WhatsApp is a genuine support channel in your market, scope and price it as its own piece of work rather than assuming it arrives with Helpdesk.

faqs.q: How is Helpdesk different from running support in Project?
faqs.a: Project gives you the queue, stages, assignment, timesheets and a portal. Helpdesk adds the SLA policy engine with per ticket status, the team level after sales actions for refunds, returns, repairs and onsite work, the customer help center and the ticket specific reporting. If nothing in your contracts mentions response times and nothing gets returned, Project may genuinely be enough.

faqs.q: Can we import our tickets from another helpdesk system?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits worth agreeing in advance. Contacts, ticket fields, tags and attachments migrate. Conversation history goes in as chatter messages. Original creation dates are not exposed by the standard import screen, so preserving them needs a scripted load, and SLA history cannot be recreated at all. Many projects import open tickets only and keep the old system readable.

faqs.q: Can customers close their own tickets?
faqs.a: That is an option on the team. When it is on, a portal user gets a close action on their ticket and it moves to the stage you nominate. Teams switch it off when closing triggers billing or a satisfaction survey they want to control, or when a second pair of eyes is required before anything is called resolved.

faqs.q: Does Odoo Helpdesk include call centre features?
faqs.a: Not in that sense. Standard Odoo has no automatic call distribution, no IVR and no supervisor wallboard. Calls can be logged against a ticket and a telephony integration can open the record on an incoming call, but a desk measured on queue time and abandonment rate needs a telephony platform beside Odoo, integrated to it rather than replaced by it.

There is no escalation matrix as a product feature. A breached SLA sets the status on the ticket and shows in reporting, but it notifies nobody on its own. Escalation is assembled from stages, automation rules that reassign or send mail, and scheduled activities with a named owner. Define what your contract means by escalation, then build exactly that.

faqs.q: Can one database serve several brands or legal entities?
faqs.a: Yes. Teams belong to a company, so each entity gets its own teams, aliases, stages and SLA policies, and record rules keep the ticket lists apart. Agents working across entities need the right companies enabled on their user. Mail templates, the portal and the help center need per company branding checked, because it does not follow automatically from the company record.
